findings.description: Default build-arg NEXTAUTH_SECRET=secret is baked into image ENV (L29); a predictable session/JWT secret enables auth token forgery if not overridden at build time.
Default build-arg CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY=secret is baked into image ENV (L30); a predictable app-data key allows decryption of stored credentials if left unchanged.
Hardcoded default Postgres credentials in the compose template (POSTGRES_USER L20, POSTGRES_PASSWORD L21); reused deployments expose the database to trivial credential guessing.
symmetricEncrypt uses AES-256-CBC (ALGORITHM=aes256) with no MAC/auth tag and a latin1 key buffer (L16); unauthenticated ciphertext is malleable and padding-oracle-prone. GCM keyring exists.
Base image pinned to mutable tag node:20 in all three stages (L1 builder, L53 builder-two, L77 runner); builds are non-reproducible and subject to silent base-image drift.
No USER directive in any build or runner stage; the production runner (L77) executes as root, so any app-level RCE runs with full in-container root privileges.
Third-party action lingodotdev/lingo.dev@main is pinned to a mutable branch; a compromised or force-pushed branch executes arbitrary code in CI with repo and secret access.
GitHub Actions are pinned to mutable major tags (e.g. actions/checkout@v4) across ~59 workflows; only 6 uses are SHA-pinned, exposing CI to tag-repoint supply-chain tampering.
Production script-src keeps 'unsafe-inline' and https: alongside nonce and strict-dynamic; browsers ignoring strict-dynamic can execute injected inline scripts.
Development CSP script-src allows 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval'; weak posture in non-production and a real risk if a dev or preview build is publicly exposed.
style-src retains 'unsafe-inline' (no style nonces); permits injected inline styles enabling CSS-based UI-redress and data-exfiltration vectors.
shouldEnforceCsp emits CSP only for /auth/login and /login; report-only mode is disabled (csp.ts L46-47), so all other routes ship with no Content-Security-Policy header.
X-Cal-Signature-256 HMAC header is set only when a subscriber secret exists (createWebhookSignature returns empty otherwise, L347-350); webhooks without a secret are sent unsigned.
API v2 enforces auth via NestJS ApiAuthGuard while v1 (pages/api) uses opt-in next-api-middleware; a guard or validation present in one version may be absent in the other.
API v1 reads the API key from the query string (req.query.apiKey), exposing the credential in URLs, server and proxy logs, and Referer headers; v2 passes it via headers.
v1 authorization is per-route opt-in via next-api-middleware label(); a handler omitting verifyApiKey/rateLimitApiKey ships with no auth or rate limit, with no global guard.
CORS origin falls back to wildcard '*' outside production when ALLOWED_ORIGINS is unset, while Authorization and secret headers are allowed; production defaults to false.
Origin allowlist converts wildcard '*' to a '.*' regex without restricting separators; overly broad patterns can match unintended attacker-controlled hosts or subdomains.
Rate limiter fails open: onError returns success:true on any error (L55); the 5s timeout fallback (L44) and missing UNKEY_ROOT_KEY (L41) also return success, silently bypassing limits.
safeGet swallows all edge-config errors in an empty catch and returns undefined; feature flags such as isSignupDisabled fail open when Edge Config is unavailable.
